extraction_scope: Worker-6 bounded mechanism adjudication from paper-local source text. Claims are phenotypic/mechanism-context claims only; no unperformed direct membrane or molecular-target assay is promoted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: NCR094 and NCR992 exhibit peptide-dependent bactericidal phenotypes against K. pneumoniae in in vitro killing assays, while MRSA activity is negligible for wild-type peptides under the tested conditions.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Killing phenotype only; the paper does not perform a direct molecular target or membrane permeabilization assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Crystal violet assays show antibiofilm phenotypes for selected NCR094/NCR992 variants against K. pneumoniae biofilm formation at subinhibitory concentration.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: NCR094.3, NCR992.1, NCR992.2, NCR992.3 and related wild-type comparators
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm biomass reduction does not identify a direct antibiofilm molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Hemolysis and K562 MTT assays define human-cell toxicity/safety context for the peptide variants; they are toxicity endpoints rather than antimicrobial mechanism assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: NCR094/NCR992 wild type and derivative panel
mechanism_claims.limitations: Dose-response supplement figures are image/PDF only; exact non-prose bar heights were not fabricated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper discusses Gram-negative/Gram-positive envelope differences and peptide physicochemical properties as plausible explanations for activity differences.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Discussion-level interpretation for NCR094/NCR992 activity patterns
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is author discussion and literature context, not direct experimental proof of membrane disruption in this study.
